chunks: Al-Bazawfari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave woman of a people unlawfully, then buys her and claims her child, then he is not inherited from him. For the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the fornicator is the stone.' And he does not inherit the child of fornication except a man who claims the son of his slave woman."

key_terms.اَلْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child belongs to the bed (principle of paternity)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a child born from a man's illicit relation with a slave woman he later buys?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance dynamics for a man who commits illicit relations with a slave woman and subsequently purchases her, ruling that the child does not inherit from him as a legitimate offspring due to the maxim 'The child belongs to the bed.' It distinguishes this from the general rule by specifying that such a man can only claim inheritance rights if he explicitly acknowledges the child as his own from that specific slave, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the distinction between *firash* (bed/marriage) and *zina* (fornication) in lineage attribution.
